extracted.intended_audience: State environmental agencies preparing State plans to implement EPA emission guidelines; EPA regional administrators; affected EGU owners/operators and compliance planners
extracted.subtask_short: state plan for EGU emission guidelines
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting a State plan to implement EPA emission guidelines for affected electric generating units (EGUs), including defining standards of performance, monitoring/recordkeeping, alternate standard forms, applicability, exclusions, compliance dates, and documentation requirements. Covers technical calculation methods and administrative submission/revision procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of standard of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard of performance for an affected EGU may take the following forms: (1) A rate-based standard of performance for an individual affected EGU that does not exceed the level calculated through the use of the methods described in § 60.5775b(c) and (d). (2) A standard of performance in an alternate form, which may apply for affected EGUs in the long-term coal-fired steam generating unit subcategory or the medium-term coal-fired steam generating unit subcategory, as provided for in § 60.5775b(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may choose the presumptively approvable individual rate-based standard or use alternate aggregate, mass-based, or trading-program forms subject to additional specified requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard must be quantifiable
rubrics_metrics.description: An affected EGU's standard of performance is quantifiable if it can be reliably measured in a manner that can be replicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plan submittal must include the methods by which the standard is quantifiable (e.g., measurement approaches and calculation methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard must be verifiable
rubrics_metrics.description: An affected EGU's standard of performance is verifiable if adequate monitoring, recordkeeping and reporting requirements are in place to enable the State and the Administrator to independently evaluate, measure, and verify compliance with the standard of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plan must specify monitoring/recordkeeping/reporting required to enable independent verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard must be non-duplicative
rubrics_metrics.description: An affected EGU's standard of performance is non-duplicative with respect to a State plan if it is not already incorporated as a standard of performance in the State plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plan must demonstrate the standard isn't already incorporated elsewhere in the plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard must be permanent
rubrics_metrics.description: An affected EGU's standard of performance is permanent if the standard of performance must be met continuously unless it is replaced by another standard of performance in an approved State plan revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans should not provide temporary or intermittent standards unless superseded via approved revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard must be enforceable
rubrics_metrics.description: An affected EGU's standard of performance is enforceable if: (i) technically accurate limitation or requirement and time period are specified; (ii) compliance requirements are clearly defined; (iii) affected EGUs are responsible for compliance and liable for violations; (iv) each compliance activity or measure is enforceable as a practical matter (per 40 CFR 49.167); and (v) Administrator, State, and third parties maintain ability to enforce and secure corrective actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plan must include specific limitations, compliance definitions, liability provisions, practical enforceability, and mechanisms for enforcement by federal, state, and third parties (including citations to applicable CAA sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptively approvable standard — long-term coal-fired units
rubrics_metrics.description: For long-term coal-fired steam generating units: (i) BSER is CCS with 90 percent capture of CO2; (ii) Degree of emission limitation is 88.4 percent reduction in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross); (iii) Presumptively approvable standard of performance is an emission rate limit defined by an 88.4 percent reduction in annual emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross) from the unit-specific baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States adopting presumptively approvable standards should apply BSER and degree-of-limitation values as specified; baseline calculation methods in § 60.5775b(d) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptively approvable standard — medium-term coal-fired units
rubrics_metrics.description: For medium-term coal-fired steam generating units: (i) BSER is natural gas co-firing at 40 percent of the heat input; (ii) Degree of emission limitation is a 16 percent reduction in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross); (iii) Presumptively approvable standard is an emission rate limit defined by a 16 percent reduction in annual emission rate from the unit-specific baseline; (iv) States must account for any preexisting co-firing reflected in the baseline and adjust the degree of emission limitation accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If baseline includes preexisting co-firing (e.g., 10%), reduce the incremental degree of limitation accordingly (example: adjusted to 12%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptively approvable standard — base load oil-fired units
rubrics_metrics.description: For base load oil-fired steam generating units: (i) BSER is routine methods of operation and maintenance; (ii) Degree of emission limitation is a 0 percent increase in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross); (iii) Presumptively approvable standard is an annual emission rate limit of 1,400 lb CO2/MWh-gross.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States using presumptively approvable standards should apply the numeric annual emission rate limit specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptively approvable standard — intermediate load oil-fired units
rubrics_metrics.description: For intermediate load oil-fired steam generating units: (i) BSER is routine methods of operation and maintenance; (ii) Degree of emission limitation is a 0 percent increase; (iii) Presumptively approvable standard is an annual emission rate limit of 1,600 lb CO2/MWh-gross.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptively approvable standard — low load oil-fired units
rubrics_metrics.description: For low load oil-fired steam generating units: (i) BSER is uniform fuels; (ii) Degree of emission limitation is 170 lb CO2/MMBtu; (iii) Presumptively approvable standard is an annual emission rate limit of 170 lb CO2/MMBtu.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptively approvable standard — base load natural gas-fired units
rubrics_metrics.description: For base load natural gas-fired steam generating units: (i) BSER is routine methods of operation and maintenance; (ii) Degree of emission limitation is a 0 percent increase; (iii) Presumptively approvable standard is an annual emission rate limit of 1,400 lb CO2/MWh-gross.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptively approvable standard — intermediate load natural gas-fired units
rubrics_metrics.description: For intermediate load natural gas-fired steam generating units: (i) BSER is routine methods of operation and maintenance; (ii) Degree of emission limitation is a 0 percent increase; (iii) Presumptively approvable standard is an annual emission rate limit of 1,600 lb CO2/MWh-gross.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptively approvable standard — low load natural gas-fired units
rubrics_metrics.description: For low load natural gas-fired steam generating units: (i) BSER is uniform fuels; (ii) Degree of emission limitation is 130 lb CO2/MMBtu; (iii) Presumptively approvable standard is an annual emission rate limit of 130 lb CO2/MMBtu.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for establishing unit-specific baseline
rubrics_metrics.description: A State shall use the CO2 mass emissions and corresponding electricity generation (or, for low-load oil- or natural gas-fired subcategory, heat input data) from the most representative continuous 8-quarter period from 40 CFR part 75 reporting within the 5-year period immediately prior to May 9, 2024. Divide total CO2 emissions (lbs) by total gross electricity generation (MWh) or total heat input (MMBtu) over that period to calculate baseline CO2 emission performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must identify the most representative continuous 8-quarter period within the specified 5-year window and document calculations and data sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate rate-based standard requirements (alternate form)
rubrics_metrics.description: If your State plan includes an aggregate rate-based standard (lb CO2/MWh-gross) for a group of affected EGUs sharing owner/operator, on a gross generation weighted average basis, the State plan must include: (1) the presumptively approvable rate-based standard for each affected EGU; (2) documentation of assumptions underlying the aggregate calculation; (3) process for calculating the aggregate gross generation weighted average emission rate each compliance period; (4) measures to implement and enforce the annual aggregate standard, including basis for determining owner/operator compliance and provisions for ownership changes; (5) demonstration that aggregate application achieves equivalent or better emission reduction than applying individual rate-based standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State must provide calculation methods, assumptions, enforcement measures, and equivalency demonstration to justify aggregate approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass-based annual limit for individual EGU requirements (alternate form)
rubrics_metrics.description: If your State plan includes an annual limit on allowable mass CO2 emissions for an individual affected EGU, the State plan must include: (1) the presumptively approvable rate-based standard that would apply to the EGU; (2) the utilization level used to calculate the mass limit and underlying data/assumptions; (3) measures to implement and enforce the annual mass limit, including assurance of equivalent performance; (4) demonstration of equivalent or better emission reduction relative to the rate-based standard; (5) the backstop rate-based emission rate requirement to be applied annually; (6) for long-term coal-fired subcategory, in lieu of (2),(4),(5) may include a presumptively approvable mass CO2 limit based on rate-based standard multiplied by utilization corresponding to 80% annual capacity factor with backstop rate equivalent to 80% reduction in baseline performance on annual basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State must include utilization assumptions, data, enforcement measures, backstop requirements, and equivalency demonstration (special 80% capacity factor option for long-term coal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate-based standard implemented through rate-based emission trading program requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where implemented through a rate-based emission trading program, State plan must include: (1) the presumptively approvable rate-based standard for each participating EGU; (2) measures to implement and enforce the trading program, including basis for awarding compliance instruments (denoted in 1 ton CO2) to EGUs that perform better and process for surrendering instruments by EGUs that exceed their rate-based standard; (3) demonstration that use of trading program will achieve equivalent or better emission reduction than individual rate-based standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program design must specify instrument award/surrender rules, enforcement, and equivalency demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass-based standard implemented through mass-based emission trading program requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where implemented through a mass-based CO2 emission trading program (surrender of allowances equal to reported mass CO2 emissions), State plan must include: (1) the presumptively approvable rate-based standard for each participating EGU; (2) calculation of mass CO2 budget contribution for each EGU (assumed utilization × presumptively approvable rate) with underlying data/assumptions; (3) measures to implement and enforce the annual budget, including assurance of equivalent emission performance; (4) demonstration that application of the CO2 budget will achieve equivalent or better emission performance than the rate-based standard; (5) the backstop rate-based emission rate requirement applied annually to each participating EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State must provide budget calculations, data, enforcement measures, equivalency demonstration, and backstop rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electric grid reliability exception documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply a less stringent standard or longer compliance schedule based on electric grid reliability, State must provide: (1) analysis of the reliability risk demonstrating the EGU is critical to maintaining electric reliability and that requiring compliance would trigger non-compliance with mandatory FERC-approved reliability standards or increase loss-of-load expectation beyond regional targets, including projection of period of reliability criticality and substantiation for requested relief (consistent with 40 CFR 60.24a(e)); (2) analysis by relevant reliability planning authority corroborating asserted reliability risk and confirming period of criticality; (3) certification from the reliability planning authority that the claims are accurate and the identified reliability problem exists and requires the specific relief requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliability claims require corroboration and formal certification by reliability planning authority and must link to specific mandatory reliability standards and regional planning targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance dates and compliance periods to include
rubrics_metrics.description: State plan must include compliance dates: (1) Long-term coal-fired subcategory must require compliance starting no later than January 1, 2032, unless a later date is applied pursuant to § 60.24a(e)-(h); (2) Medium-term coal-fired and oil- and natural gas-fired subcategories (base, intermediate, low load) must require compliance starting no later than January 1, 2030, unless a later date is applied pursuant to § 60.24a(e)-(h). The State plan must require affected EGUs to achieve compliance for each compliance period as defined in § 60.5880b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may request later compliance dates only through the specified reliability provisions; plans must define compliance periods per § 60.5880b.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan submission timing and electronic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit a State plan or a negative declaration letter with the information required under § 60.5740b by May 11, 2026. All information must be submitted according to the electronic reporting requirements in § 60.5875b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late or non-electronic submissions are not compliant; follow specified electronic reporting formats and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for revising an EPA-approved State plan
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA-approved State plans can be revised only with approval by the Administrator. The Administrator will approve a State plan revision if it is satisfactory with respect to the applicable requirements of this subpart and all applicable requirements of subpart Ba. If one or more State plan elements in § 60.5740b require revision, the State must submit a revision pursuant to § 60.28a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plan revisions require Administrator approval and must follow § 60.28a submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA commitment to review emission guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will review and, if appropriate, revise these emission guidelines as they apply to coal-fired affected EGUs by January 1, 2041; EPA need not review if Administrator determines review is not appropriate in light of readily available information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a commitment, not an automatic requirement; EPA retains discretion based on available information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of subpart to EGU owners/operators and federal plan fallback
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart does not directly affect EGU owners or operators in your State, except as provided in § 60.5710b(b). However, affected EGU owners/operators must comply with the State plan developed to implement the emission guidelines. If a State does not submit a State plan by May 11, 2026, or EPA disapproves a State plan, EPA will implement and enforce a Federal plan (§ 60.5720b) applicable to each affected EGU within the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State choices determine whether owners/operators are subject to State or Federal plan implementation/enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: EGUs that must be addressed in the State plan
rubrics_metrics.description: State plan must address: (1) any affected EGUs that were in operation or had commenced construction on or before January 8, 2014; (2) coal-fired steam generating units that commenced a modification on or before May 23, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must identify units meeting these date-based applicability triggers and include them in the plan unless excluded under § 60.5850b.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of affected EGU
rubrics_metrics.description: An affected EGU is a steam generating unit that: (1) serves a generator capable of selling greater than 25 MW to a utility power distribution system; and (2) has a base load rating (design heat input capacity) greater than 260 GJ/hr (250 MMBtu/hr) heat input of fossil fuel (alone or combined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these thresholds to determine whether a unit qualifies as an affected EGU for State plan coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded EGUs from being affected
rubrics_metrics.description: EGUs excluded from being affected include: (a) New or reconstructed units subject to subpart TTTT due to commencing construction after TTTT applicability date; (b) Modified natural gas- or oil-fired units subject to subpart TTTT due to modification after applicability date; (c) Modified coal-fired units subject to subpart TTTTa due to modification after applicability date; (d) EGUs subject to federally enforceable permit limiting net-electric sales to ≤1/3 of potential output or ≤219,000 MWh annually (and have never exceeded that); (e) Non-fossil fuel units capable of ≥50% non-fossil heat input and with federally enforceable permit limiting fossil fuel use to ≤10% of annual capacity factor; (f) CHP units with federally enforceable permit limiting annual net-electric sales to ≤219,000 MWh or product of design efficiency and potential output; (g) Units that serve a generator along with other EGUs where prorated effective generation capacity is ≤25 MW; (h) Municipal waste combustors subject to 40 CFR part 60, subpart Eb; (i) Commercial/industrial solid waste incineration units subject to 40 CFR part 60, subpart CCCC; (j) EGUs deriving >50% heat input from an industrial process that does not produce external electrical/mechanical/useful thermal output; (k) Existing coal-fired units that have demonstrated plans to permanently cease operations before January 1, 2032, per § 60.5740b(a)(9)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must apply these exclusion categories when determining affected-unit inventories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring plan requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator of an affected EGU required to meet standards must prepare a monitoring plan in accordance with 40 CFR 75.53(g) and (h), unless such a plan already exists under another program that requires CO2 mass emissions to be monitored and reported according to 40 CFR part 75.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring plans must satisfy Part 75 certification/QA requirements or reference an existing compliant plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'valid operating hours' and 'valid data' for rate-based standards
rubrics_metrics.description: For rate-based standards, only 'valid operating hours' count — full or partial operating hours for which: (i) 'valid data' (as defined in § 60.5880b) are obtained for all parameters used to determine hourly CO2 mass emissions (lbs) (substitute data from part 75, flow monitoring bias adjustments, or data from instruments failing required relative accuracy audit frequency are not 'valid data'); and (ii) the corresponding hourly gross energy output value is also valid (zero is valid for hours with no useful output).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States and owners/operators must follow the strict valid-data rules when determining hours used in rate calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure and report hourly CO2 mass emissions via CEMS or O2 monitor — procedures and QA
rubrics_metrics.description: For rate-based standards, owners/operators must measure and report hourly CO2 mass emissions using procedures: (i) install/certify/operate/maintain/calibrate a CO2 CEMS and exhaust gas flow rate monitoring system per 40 CFR 75.10(a)(3)(i), or alternatively use a certified O2 monitor to calculate CO2 concentration provided the EGU does not use carbon separation (and account for non-combustion CO2 if controls produce it); (ii) calculate hourly CO2 mass emission rate per specified equations/appendices depending on wet/dry basis; (iii) multiply hourly tons/hr by operating time and convert to lbs; (iv) record hourly CO2 tons/hr and operating times under 40 CFR 75.57(e) and report electronically under 40 CFR 75.64(a)(6) if required; (v) sum hourly CO2 mass emissions; (vi) monitoring system must meet certification and QA procedures in 40 CFR 75.20 and appendices A and B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Part 75 CEMS certification, QA, equation references (appendices F, G), and recording/reporting requirements; treat substitute or biased data as invalid for rate calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative calculation for liquid/gaseous fuel-only units (heat input method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators that exclusively combust liquid and/or gaseous fuel may determine hourly CO2 mass emissions by: (i) implementing procedures in appendix D to part 75 to determine hourly heat input rates from fuel flow and gross calorific value, using certified fuel flow meters and fuel GCV determinations; (ii) using Equation G-4 in appendix G to calculate hourly CO2 mass emission rate (tons/hr); (iii) converting hourly tons/hr to lbs by multiplying by operating time and 2,000 lbs/ton; (iv) recording and reporting hourly CO2 tons/hr and operating times under 40 CFR 75.57(e) and 75.64(a)(6); (v) summing hourly CO2 mass emissions; (vi) owners may determine site-specific carbon-based F-factors (Fc) per Equation F-7b in appendix F and use in calculations instead of default Fc values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This alternative relies on fuel-based measurements and appropriate meter/GCV certification and may use site-specific F-factors with Administrator petition per Part 75 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross energy output measurement (watt meters) and calculation of P_gross/net
rubrics_metrics.description: For rate-based standards, owners/operators must install/calibrate/maintain/operate sufficient watt meters to continuously measure and record on an hourly basis gross electric output using 0.2 accuracy class instrumentation per ANSI C12.20-2010. Combined heat and power facilities must also measure useful thermal and mechanical output where applicable. Procedures to calculate P_gross/net (hourly gross or net energy output in MWh) are specified, including handling hours with zero output, conversion to MWh, summation of P_gross/net for valid operating hours, and dividing total CO2 mass emissions by summed P_gross/net to determine CO2 emissions rate (lb/MWh). Definitions and equation components (PE_ST, PE_CT, PE_IE, PE_A, PT_PS, PT_HR, PT_IE, TDF) are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specified equation and component definitions; apply TDF and CHPspecifc PT_PS calculation where applicable; follow Part 75 reporting to convert to MWh and aggregate over valid operating hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common stack monitoring and multi-stack monitoring rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more affected EGUs that implement continuous emissions monitoring share a common exhaust stack and are subject to the same emissions standard, the owner/operator may monitor the hourly CO2 mass emissions at the common stack instead of monitoring each EGU separately; the hourly gross or net output for the stack must be the sum of individual outputs and operating time expressed as 'stack operating hours' (§ 60.13(g)). If exhaust gases are emitted through multiple stacks (or monitored in ducts), hourly CO2 mass emissions and stack operating time at each stack/duct must be monitored separately and compliance determined by summing CO2 mass emissions and dividing by gross/net energy output for the affected EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting common-stack monitoring requires summing outputs appropriately and using stack operating hours; multiple-stack situations require separate monitoring and aggregation of emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment when EGUs serve a common generator
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more affected EGUs serve a common electric generator, apportion the combined hourly gross or net energy output to individual affected EGUs according to the fraction of total steam load contributed by each EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must require and document the apportionment method consistent with steam-load fractions to attribute generation for compliance determinations.
